core.title: Declare each user/system flow participant once as a typed participant id
core.given: A user/system flow definition (a plan artifact) whose actors — processing components, human roles, external systems and data sources — are declared as participants
core.when: The planner authors, edits or checks that user/system flow definition's participant declarations
core.then: List each participant exactly once as a typed participant id: one of the profile's participant-type prefixes (processing component, human actor, external system or data source) followed by its id, matching the profile's participant-id pattern.
prefer: Use the processing participant type for a component that performs processing, the human participant type for a human actor's role, and the external participant type for an external system or data source
Shape each id part according to the participant id-part syntax declared by the profile
avoid: Listing the same participant more than once
Using a participant type other than the profile's declared participant types, or omitting the type
An id part that does not conform to the profile's participant id-part syntax
Typing a human actor or an external source as a processing participant (or the reverse)
core.why: User/system flow steps move artifacts between declared participants, so a uniquely named, typed actor list keeps every step's source and destination unambiguous and checkable.
evidence: Every entry in the user/system flow definition's participants list matches the profile's participant-id pattern
No participant string appears more than once in the list
Each participant's type matches its role: the processing type marks a component that performs processing, the human type a human actor, the external type an external system or data source
verification: Check every entry in a user/system flow definition's participants list against the profile's participant-id pattern; entries that do not match are findings.
Uniqueness is checked on exact participant strings: each participant is listed once, and exact string duplicates are findings.
The pattern check flags only entries outside the profile's pattern; id-part shapes the pattern still accepts (for example repeated or trailing hyphens where the pattern allows them) are not findings.

Whether a participant's type matches its actual role (processing component, human actor, external system or data source) is semantic evidence checked in review; the mechanical check covers pattern and uniqueness only.

Activation on file kind needs an observer that classifies plan artifacts as user/system flow definitions; scope is any such definition that is authored, edited or reviewed, whichever part of it changes.

fires: Planner authors a new user/system flow definition and lists its participants
Planner adds a processing component, human role or external source to an existing user/system flow's participants
Planner edits any part of an existing user/system flow definition (for example its steps) whose participant declarations must still conform
Planner or reviewer checks a user/system flow's participant declarations
doesNotFire: Editing a processing component's own internal artifacts without touching or checking any user/system flow definition
Code-level changes that do not touch planning artifacts

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds that the file_kind activation and the rule's scope refer to; in this stack, the workflow (user/system flow) definition kind.

The participant-id grammar of a user/system flow definition: the typed prefix for each participant type (processing component, human actor, external system or data source) and the id-part syntax, i.e. the combined validation pattern used by the obligation and its check.
profileRequirements.bunValue: product capability -> capability:{capability-id} (performs processing); user -> user:{role} (human actor); system -> system:{source} (external system/data source); validation pattern ^(product capability|user|system):[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$

neutralityNotes: The concrete participant-id grammar — the type prefixes capability:/user:/system: and the validation regex — is stack data with no existing vocabulary key, so it is carried by the proposed key urn.participant and the core speaks only of participant types and the profile's participant-id pattern. 'user/system flow' and 'participant' are ATDD-method planning vocabulary shared across stacks (the closed vocabulary itself lists user/system flow as an artifact param), so they remain in the core; the concrete plan-artifact kind name comes from roles.plan_artifact.kinds. 'product capability' as an actor type is neutralized to 'processing participant / component'. bun.json declares no severity, disposition or exceptions (unless is empty), so the core's verification adds none. The file-kind activation still needs a new observer; that gap is preserved verbatim.
